A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REVA-PO study, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 ends after its references; v2 includes Supplementary Material A–H. The retained material and supplementary additions support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray results, training-stage and RL-component ablations, training curves, and generated-report examples in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and additionally reports reward comparisons, group-size and model-size analyses, computational measurements, and classifier performance.

M1.justification: The three-stage pipeline, RER weighting, VAPR resets, BLEU-4 reward, and Algorithm 1 are retained. The supplement provides implementation details and evaluates alternative configurations without establishing a revision to the proposed optimization procedure.

E1.justification: The work continues to use MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray. Supplementary experiments examine the existing report-generation pipeline and its classifier component. External datasets listed in Table S9 describe prior methods' resources, rather than newly evaluated datasets for REVA-PO.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. Appendix A adds comparisons with alternative reward-based training: Table S5 includes a RadGraph-F1-reward policy, and Appendix A.1 reports collapse when training with CheXpert F1.

E3.justification: The supplement adds several evaluation designs: reward-agreement metrics, classifier AUC evaluation, group sizes 4–6 on A100 GPUs, and 3B-versus-7B comparisons, with 12 versus 9 MIMIC-CXR RL epochs. The main benchmark splits and metrics remain unchanged; newly disclosed settings for existing runs do not establish that those runs changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained pipeline and RL-component ablations, v2 supplies reward-choice and reward-inversion analyses, pre/post-RL reward alignment, computational-overhead measurements, group-size sensitivity, model-size comparisons, and classifier diagnostics. These substantially broaden the evidence about stability, design choices, and resource requirements.

E5.justification: Figures S5 and S9 add descriptive variability reporting through within-group reward standard deviations and mean/standard-deviation curves for response-level KL weights. These concern response variability; neither version supplies repeated-training-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–4 retain their results, while the supplement adds substantial numerical and qualitative evidence. For example, Table S5 newly reports CheXpert F1 0.480 and RadGraph F1 0.259 for RadGraph-reward training; Table S7 adds 3B results. Reward agreement, group-size outcomes, classifier AUCs, and computational costs are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces mathematical definitions of sign-consistency probability and top-1 selection consistency in Equations 11–12. The original method equations and algorithm remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about RER/VAPR stability, the efficient three-stage LVLM pipeline, and state-of-the-art report quality. The headline improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The supplement attributes CheXpert-reward instability to high variance and RadGraph reward inversion to entity stuffing, and interprets reward agreement as linguistic–clinical alignment. It also adds explanations of model-size effects, computational constraints, and classifier replacement requirements, substantially extending the interpretation of the retained method.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D supply exact prompts, optimizer and LoRA settings, stage-specific training budgets, policy-update intervals, classifier-label processing, and the 10,000-example MIMIC-CXR RL subset selected after filtering short reports. Hardware and computational details are expanded. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility without establishing changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: Appendix H and Table S9 add systematic positioning against prior methods by backbone size, external data, dense annotations, knowledge graphs, and evaluation-data modifications. This introduces a substantial resource-efficiency and comparison-fairness argument, supported by additional references, while retaining the main related-work discussion.

P1.justification: The existing abstract and Sections 1–5 remain essentially verbatim and retain their order. v2 adds acknowledgements and an organized A–H supplement, but does not substantially rewrite or reorganize the original narrative.

P2.justification: The original figures and tables retain their displays. v2 adds reward-distribution plots, a reward-inversion example, prompt examples, stability curves, and Tables S5–S9 covering supplementary results and prior-method resources. These substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 refers readers to reward justification and implementation details absent from its PDF. v2 supplies that evidence and a detailed training recipe, resolving substantial support and reproducibility gaps while preserving the main results. Stage 3 classifier use remains ambiguously described across Figure 1 and Appendix C, but this limitation does not outweigh the substantial gains in completeness and assessability.
